items.title: Patagonia's owner gave the company to the planet
items.claim: In September 2022, Yvon Chouinard announced he was transferring ownership of Patagonia. What was the structure?

options.text: An IPO on the New York Stock Exchange
All voting stock to the Patagonia Purpose Trust (climate-aligned governance); all non-voting stock (98%) to the Holdfast Collective, with future profits funding environmental causes
A sale to a private equity buyer

items.reveal:
Chouinard, his wife Malinda and their two children transferred Patagonia (valued around $3bn) using two vehicles: the Purpose Trust holds voting control to ensure mission alignment; the Holdfast Collective (a 501(c)(4) nonprofit) holds economic ownership and receives roughly $100m of annual profits to fund environmental work.

The structure required the family to pay $17.5m in gift tax. The company is a B Corp (certified since 2011) — the legal structure goes much further than B Corp certification alone.

B Lab's B Corp movement, launched in 2006, certifies firms meeting social and environmental performance standards.
items.why: Corporate ownership structures shape objectives. A trust-owned firm doesn't have to maximise shareholder returns — because its 'shareholders' are not the same as a public company's.

items.title: UK Supreme Court ruled Uber drivers were workers, not self-employed
items.claim: In February 2021, the UK Supreme Court ruled on the employment status of Uber drivers. What did it decide?

options.text: Drivers were correctly classified as self-employed
Drivers were 'workers' under UK law, entitled to minimum wage, paid holiday and pension auto-enrolment
Drivers were 'employees' with full unfair-dismissal rights
Uber was banned from operating in the UK

items.reveal:
The case ran from a 2016 Employment Tribunal decision to the Supreme Court. Lord Leggatt's judgment held that Uber's contract terms could not displace the reality of control: Uber set fares, terms, the rating system and routes.

Uber subsequently announced UK drivers would be paid minimum wage and pension contributions. The judgment did not give drivers full 'employee' status (no protection against unfair dismissal). Similar litigation has run in California, France and the Netherlands.
items.why: UK employment law has three statuses (employee, worker, self-employed). The 'worker' middle category was created in 1996; gig economy litigation has been the main test of where the line falls.

items.title: ROCE compares like with like across firm sizes
items.claim: A firm has operating profit of £2 million, total assets of £15 million and current liabilities of £5 million. What is ROCE?
items.reveal_title: Operating profit divided by capital employed
items.reveal:
Capital employed = total assets - current liabilities = £15m - £5m = £10m. ROCE = £2m / £10m = 20%.

ROCE is the most commonly cited single profitability measure in UK A-level. It is benchmarked against the cost of capital — if a firm consistently earns less than its weighted cost of capital, it is destroying shareholder value. UK FTSE 100 firms have averaged 10-15% ROCE over the last decade.
items.why: Absolute profit figures don't tell you whether capital was well used. A £2m profit from £10m of capital is 20%; the same profit from £100m of capital is 2%.
